notes: GRADE LOCKED TO C. The grade letter selects REFERENCE GAIN as well as reset state - A/B are gain 1 (2.500V full scale), C/D are gain 2 (5.000V). This row previously read 'DAC8568C (or A grade)' and explained the letter as reset state only. C also clears to ZERO scale where B/D clear to midscale and would park pitch octaves up. Populate 6 of 8: pitch, 4 mods, mod offset; channels 6 and 8 spare. Internal ref DISABLED by default, enable at boot. description: Current-limited hot-swap controller on the umbilical +12V feed
notes: REPLACES TPS2553, a 2.5-6.5V USB switch with a 7V abs max that would not survive first power-on at 12V. Suffix matters: -1 LATCHES OFF, -2 auto-retries. THE FET IS NOT SOT-23 - that was an SOA error. A 1.0A ramp at ~6V mean for 75ms is ~6W and 0.45J; SOT-23 transient thermal impedance at that pulse width gives hundreds of degrees of junction rise. Choose a DPAK or SO-8 part against its SINGLE-PULSE SOA CURVE, and program the LT1641's FOLDBACK, which exists to hold FET dissipation roughly constant in current limit. Set the limit at 1.0A with a programmed 50-100ms ramp. LM5069MM or LTC4210 equally valid

notes: Edge-lit

notes: Full bench available - E9 not gated on tooling

description: 5.000V precision series reference for the breath sensor supply
notes: +-0.05%, 3ppm/degC, ~5ppm/V line reg. The MPXV4006DP is ratiometric so its supply IS its scale factor. Buffered by half of U-BUF

description: Dual RRIO op-amp: breath buffer + reference buffer
notes: SOIC-8. Runs on +12V not 5V - a +12V fault on the BREATH conductor is at the rail so no clamp current, which kills the >=3.3k protection resistor requirement. SAME part as the module op-amps. STABILITY: as an unbuffered follower this drives the sensor's 100nF decoupler plus C-REF-OUT's 10uF - a pole at 21kHz (or 200Hz) INSIDE its own loop, three decades below crossover, which no general-purpose precision op-amp survives unconditionally. FIX IT INSIDE THE LOOP - isolation resistor in series with the output, feedback taken at the SENSOR PIN - the same trick the pitch stage now uses. An isolation resistor OUTSIDE the loop is not an option: 10 ohm at the sensor's ~10mA is 100mV on 5.000V, 2% of a ratiometric scale factor against a reference specified to 0.05%

description: Instrumentation amp - breath receiver, senses against AGND
notes: BREATH drives IN-, AGND drives IN+, REF is driven by TRIM-BREATH-ZERO through a BUFFER - never a bare divider, since source impedance on an in-amp REF pin degrades CMRR one-for-one. Output is 0V at rest to -9.6V at full (Vout = -2.185*(V_BREATH - V_AGND) + V_REF, with TRIM-BREATH-ZERO nulling the sensor pedestal). This field read "-0.44V at rest to -10V at full" until 2026-09-21 - that is the UN-NULLED output from before REF carried a trimmer, and trimming to it at E10 leaves the downstream stage ~1.8V off zero at the working gain; the downstream stage inverts, which is also the topology that does gain-then-offset with two pots in one op-amp half. The DAC ch6 zero injection that originally justified the input swap is deleted (ADR 0003). See hardware/module/breath-receive-stage.md

notes: ~400mm - the sensor sits at the BOTTOM with the real-time board (ADR 0003), not at the top. 1.17ms propagation, the largest single term in the latency budget. Trap <=1mL and clearable without disassembly

description: Quad buffer as LED data level shifter
notes: SOIC-14. 5V rail TTL thresholds so 3V3 reads high. Two spare gates. VERIFY WS2815 threshold

description: Level shifter, 3V3 SPI up to 5V for the DAC
notes: SAME part as the instrument LED shifter. Covers SCLK MOSI CS with a spare gate. Runs from bus +5V; the DAC runs from U-REG-DAC. OE IS TIED ENABLED. The presence-gated OE is deleted along with its comparator: the threshold sat inside the breath signal's own range, it locked out every standalone module milestone, and it failed toward 'present'. What it was protecting against - floating CMOS at the DAC while the instrument is off - is what R-SPI-PULL's six resistors are for, and running the buffer unconditionally is what every surveyed Eurorack module does

description: Eurorack power inlet
notes: Shrouded and keyed - reversed ribbon is the classic eurorack failure. Carries the +5V rail the module REQUIRES

description: Schottky reverse polarity protection
notes: ~0.3-0.4V drop. Community standard for eurorack power entry. THREE not two: the module's analog +12V and the umbilical feed must NOT share a diode - instrument current then modulates its Vf by ~80mV, which is ~20 cents of breath-correlated pitch bend and needs no ground path at all (ADR 0006) | 2026-09-21: the '20 cents of breath-correlated pitch bend' this row used to cite as the reason for the THIRD diode is refuted - the real figure is 0.00018 cents, because pitch references the DAC's INTERNAL reference and not this rail. KEEP qty 3 anyway, on the reasons that do hold: fault isolation between the exported rail and the analog rail, and HF isolation (r_d 69 mohm). Stated wrongly, the next reviewer who checks the arithmetic deletes the part.

description: Adjustable LDO set to 5.25V for the DAC AVDD
notes: Off protected +12V. ~13mA load incl. the divider, ~90mW. Decouples DAC full scale from the rack's +-5% +5V rail. TOLERANCE IS A BENCH TASK, NOT A SPEC TASK: worst case spans 0.66V against a ~0.55V window and no nominal value fits on paper, but this is one unit with a TO-92 part, two through-hole resistors and a voltmeter. E7 measures where the DAC's top codes start compressing against AVDD and selects R2 from that

description: LM317 output setting divider
notes: Vout = 1.25*(1+475/150) = 5.21V. WAS 240R/768R at 1%, whose stated '+-4% = 5.04-5.46V' ignored both the divider tolerance and I_ADJ. Smaller R2 halves the I_ADJ term to 24-48mV; 0.1% parts cost pennies in the same order. The LM317's own 1.20-1.30V reference is the dominant term and no divider fixes it - so R2 is SELECTED ON THE BENCH at E7 (this is a population of one), and the value here is the starting point. Buy a handful of neighbouring E96 values

description: LM317 ADJ bypass and output cap
notes: ADJ bypass drops output noise to ~50uV RMS. Output cap for LDO stability

description: Series bead per supply branch
notes: One per branch: +12V analog, +12V umbilical, -12V, +5V. Rated >=1A - the common 0805 600R part is ~300mA and a saturated bead is a wire. The '470uF at the load' half of this row moved out: entry bulk is C-BULK-RAIL, strip bulk is C-STRIP-BULK, and this row was double-booking them

description: Series protection on each CV output
notes: POWER RATING IS NOT OPTIONAL and the worst case moved when pitch took jack-side feedback. Pitch shorted now rails the op-amp across this resistor: 142mW. Pitch against a 220R output at -5V in output-to-output patching: 192mW steady state, because the loop FIGHTS the other module now that the jack is the feedback node. The old stated worst case (a mod at 10.05V into a short, 101mW) is no longer the worst. 250mW would be 1.3x; specify >=500mW - a high-power 1206 or a 2010. VERIFY the part exists in 1206 at 500mW; distributors were unreachable. Mutable specifies its output 1k at >=200mW where every other resistor in the same BOM is 100mW, which is the published form of this argument | 2026-09-21: RATING RAISED. Two reviewers independently found the stated worst case understated ~2x - 322mW (output-to-output against a 220R source at +/-10V) and 269/312/464mW on a fuller ladder. Thick-film derating at a 50C rack interior leaves a 500mW 1206 delivering 350-420mW, so margin was ~1.1x not 2.6x. Specify 0.66-1W 1206 (ERJ-P08 class, confirmed to exist). This is the ONLY part in the module at real risk from any jack fault

description: HF decoupling at every module IC supply pin
notes: One per supply pin, close to the pin. 6 x OPA2197 on +/-12V = 12, INA828 = 2, DAC8568 AVDD+DVDD = 2, 74AHCT125, LT1641 VCC, LM317 in. Was 22 with the 74HC123; the watchdog is deleted | 2026-09-21: was 21. The two caps counted for the LM311 are removed - that part was DELETED and its footprint is no longer drawn

description: Decoupling, one per shift register, on its cluster board
notes: One per device, on its own board - which is where it belongs. A 74x165's output edges brown out a local rail that has no reservoir

description: Anti-alias cap at the MCP3202 input pin
notes: 564Hz with the divider's 6k Thevenin (10k||15k) - matches the 500Hz channel everywhere else. WAS 220nF, which is 121Hz and smears the breath band; the '~600Hz, 58dB at 496kHz' note was wrong twice over - wrong corner, and the R-78E5.0 switches at 330kHz not 496kHz. 55dB at 330kHz. C0G not X7R in a DC-accurate path

description: 0.6x divider from the breath buffer to the ADC
notes: Sensor reaches 4.7V into a 3V3 ADC. Divide AFTER the buffer, not before. >=10k upper leg: 5V-before-3V3 sequencing otherwise pushes ~2.5mA into the ADC ESD clamp on every power-up. Needs C-AA-ADC to still settle

description: Bulk at each WS2815 feed point
notes: Bulk belongs at the load. A ferrite is a wire at the WS2815's ~2kHz PWM rate

description: LC between the umbilical node and the buck input
notes: A real inductor, not a bead. This is the part the bead was wrongly credited for

description: SPI idle-state pulls at the module
notes: SIX, not three - BOTH SIDES of the 74AHCT125. Cable side: CS to +5V, SCLK and MOSI to ground, so the buffer's inputs do not float and crowbar when the instrument is absent. DAC side: same, because with OE disabled the buffer outputs are Hi-Z and it is then the DAC's SCLK/DIN/SYNC that float - which is the state these were bought for and the three cable-side pulls do not reach. Module-alive-instrument-off is the normal state, not a fault; a stray CS edge latches garbage into the pitch DAC. CABLE-SIDE CS PULLS TO 3V3, NOT +5V: pulled to 5V it drives 430uA continuously through the unpowered ESP32's input clamp in the design's NORMAL resting state, and the node sits at ~0.7V so 'CS idle high' is not even achieved. DAC-SIDE CS PULLS TO AVDD (the LM317's 5.21V), not bus +5V - a pull-up belongs on its consumer's rail, and on the bus rail a reversed ribbon reaches the DAC's SYNC pin and turns a $0.30 buffer failure into a DAC failure

description: Series termination on SCLK, MOSI and CS at the driving end
notes: THREE. 100R, not 220R - revised 2026-09-21. 2m of Cat5 is a 100-ohm TRANSMISSION LINE (20ns round trip against 2-5ns edges), not an RC corner, and three reviewers agreed the old RC derivation was the wrong model. At 220R the far end's first step is 1.83-1.86V against the 74AHCT125's 2.0V VIH, dwelling ~20ns per edge in the forbidden band on a part with no hysteresis. 100R gives a clean 2.75V single step and 33mA of fault current; 68R is electrically ideal but draws 48mA against a 40mA pad spec. carrier.md used to draw these as R-SCLK-SER / R-MOSI-SER / R-CS-SER, which were in no BOM

description: Series resistor on each op-amp + input driven by the DAC
notes: SEVEN. Now correct on the mod channels as well, because the two-resistor form drives the op-amp's (+) input directly - a true high-Z node where 1k causes no error. It was wrong on the OLD four-resistor version, where the 10k input resistor WAS the gain network and 1k in series unbalanced it. Pitch, mod 1-4, the mod offset buffer, the VREFOUT follower. DAC on 5.21V and op-amps on +-12V do not come up together; bounds clamp current, outside the feedback path so no accuracy cost

description: Clamp diodes on the DRIVER side of R-OUT-PROT
notes: MOVED to the op-amp side of the 1k, which fixes two things at once. (a) BACK-POWERING: clamped at the JACK, a neighbouring module driving 10V through its own 220R output pushes 42mA per jack into our +12V rail when this module is off - 254mA across six jacks, into the rail that also feeds the umbilical. Behind the 1k it is 7.6mA per jack. (b) LEAKAGE: inside the feedback loop the op-amp absorbs it, so the 2.4-cent BAT54S error goes to identically zero for any diode. BAV99 kept anyway - silicon costs nothing and the reasoning no longer depends on it. NOTE: no surveyed design clamps a CV output to the RAILS at all; every clamp in the corpus goes to GND. Erica Synths is the one that puts its clamp on the driver side, which is where this now is. SIX - one per OUTPUT jack including breath, whose schematic omitted it. The two BREATH INPUT clamps are a separate row, D-CLAMP-BREATH, so the module carries eight BAV99 in total

description: Helmholtz restrictor AND liquid-water barrier at the sensor port
notes: One part, two jobs: sizes the resonance above the 500Hz corner and blocks liquid. Size the orifice at E2. Trap volume <=1mL. Pressure port only - the DP's reference port is unplumbed

description: Conformal coating for the in-body boards
notes: Breathed into for hours behind 18 unsealed switch cutouts, interior 10-20K above ambient. MASK BOTH SENSOR PORTS FIRST - a sealed reference chamber gains ~5.2kPa when warm and the output clips at zero, looking like a dead sensor (ADR 0003)

description: Bonds the aluminium plate to PWR_GND
notes: PWR_GND, never AGND. Unbonded, the plate floats 1-2mm from 18 switch pins and fires spurious notes on touch. AGND would put body capacitance on the breath reference

description: Tail window for the 8x8 matrix
notes: NOT the side panels' frosted material - needs pixel definition, not blur. Thin and close to the LEDs. Prototype at M6

description: Umbilical cable, module to instrument
notes: STRANDED not solid-core: solid core work-hardens and fractures under constant flexing, which is this cable's whole life. Shielded preferred. It is a CONSUMABLE - keep spares and replace at the first intermittency

description: Mouthpiece - no bite sensor, raw tube is playable
notes: OD must let the lips vent at the corners - that is what makes circular breathing work. Bore settled at E2 by playing two or three sizes. Removable for cleaning

description: INA828 gain-set resistor
notes: G = 1 + 50k/42.2k = 2.185. Effective 2.161 after the bias/series divider -> 9.94V jack span. The panel gain knob absorbs the 0.6%

description: Common-mode bias return, one per in-amp input
notes: REPLACES R-PD-BREATH. Without these the in-amp floats when unplugged and saturates to a rail. ~60nA against a 350mA power return = 0.2ppm, so AGND's no-current rule survives

description: Module-side series protection, one per leg
notes: Matched. Gigaohm in-amp inputs make source impedance irrelevant to CMRR, so 10k is free

description: 500Hz filter AHEAD of the in-amp
notes: 482Hz differential (NOT 531Hz - that assumed 20k of series resistance; adding R1b to the return leg makes both legs 11k). C_diff must be ~10x C_cm or a CM mismatch converts to DM. AHEAD of the amp, not after - a filter after it cannot stop RF rectification from a 2.4GHz radio 2m away

description: Breath output reconstruction cap
notes: ~480Hz with R-OUT-PROT. Film not X7R: DC bias coefficient moves the corner 30% at 10V. ON THE JACK SIDE of R-OUT-PROT, never the op-amp side - inside the loop it is a capacitive load and the stage can oscillate.

description: Sets the load switch current limit
notes: THE resistor that is the limit. 1.0A target. The stated 0.9-1.13A window is +-11% and is NARROWER THAN THE LT1641'S OWN SENSE-THRESHOLD TOLERANCE - the same mistake already found and fixed on the LM317 divider, one row down. So E6 measures the TRIP as well as the load, with a current probe, and the value is selected on the bench like R-REG-SET

description: Series protection on the breath buffer output into the umbilical
notes: TWO, not one, and 1206 not 0805 - both changed with the schematic and this row did not follow. R1 in the BREATH leg, R1b its twin in the AGND leg: the return leg carries no signal current, so a matching resistor costs no differential gain and is what keeps the 1M bias pair from capping CMRR at 60dB on its own. 1206 because ADR 0003's designed-safe sustained +12V fault puts 11.8mA through R1: 139mW against an 0805's ~125mW. Both are instrument-side and UNRETROFITTABLE

description: Reconstruction filter cap on mod 1-4 outputs
notes: 1k x 82nF = 1.94kHz. Real attenuation on the 3.6kHz ZOH image that a 15.9kHz corner ignores. FOUR not five: breath does not pass through the DAC and has its own 330nF (C-OUT-BREATH, ~480Hz). ON THE JACK SIDE of R-OUT-PROT, never the op-amp side - inside the loop it is a capacitive load and the stage can oscillate. PACKAGE IS PROBABLY WRONG: 82nF in C0G/NP0 almost certainly does not exist in 0805 - C0G permittivity puts that value in 1210 or larger. Unverified because every distributor site was proxy-blocked. Options if it is not buyable: 1210, a film part, or raise the corner and take less attenuation on the 4kHz image

description: Two-resistor non-inverting network per mod channel
notes: EIGHT, not sixteen: R1=10k, R2=30k per channel, k=3 so gain = 1+k = 4 exactly and the intercept is k x V_ref with V_ref = 3.3333V from the offset channel. Lands on EXACTLY +-10.000V, where the old four-resistor difference amp needed a 40.2k fudge to reach +-10.05. One matching requirement per channel instead of two, and the CLR-safe property survives because both terms still go to zero. Buy from one reel. See hardware/module/mod-channels.md

description: Pull-up holding the DAC8568 CLR inactive, with a bring-up pad
notes: THE WATCHDOG IS DELETED (U-WATCHDOG, R-WDT, C-WDT all gone), so CLR has no driver and is tied INACTIVE - pulled high. A solder pad to ground beside it lets CLR be asserted BY HAND, which E7-E10 want anyway: a 99ms watchdog would have fought every 'write a code, read the meter' step of pitch calibration. Leave the DAC's clear-code register at its default so a manual CLR still parks at zero scale. Do NOT write ClearIgnore

description: ORs USB VBUS with the umbilical-derived 5V rail for bench use
notes: One diode per source into the shared 5V node. Both sources drop ~0.3V, leaving ~4.7V at the dev boards' 5V pins - fine for their onboard LDOs, and the breath sensor is no longer on this rail. Bench affordance for E5, explicitly not a standalone mode

description: Passive carrier: dev board headers, ADC, reference, buffers, level shifter, power entry, service header
notes: Must carry the ~22mm cutout under the 8x8 matrix (ADR 0014), the umbilical backing-plate mounting and the service header (ADR 0009). Impossible to add later. The key-scan front end is NOT here - the registers and their 63 passives live on the cluster boards, which takes ~41% of area off a two-layer board that a review costed at ~82% covered with a 22mm hole through it. Nothing on it is fast or RF - 2 layers, hand-assembled

description: DAC, scaling, jacks, power entry, load switch
notes: Must brace the etherCON mechanically. 10HP, via 8HP, not 6HP: the 23.8mm hole leaves 8.27mm of panel each side at 40.34mm (ADR 0004) | 2026-09-21: 8HP -> 10HP, so the board widens ~35mm to ~45mm. The etherCON notch is now a smaller fraction of the board, which eases the 4.5mm web a review flagged. 'watchdog' is struck from this row's description - that part is DELETED

part: 2.54mm female header strip - machined or dual-wipe
description: Sockets for both dev boards on the carrier
notes: Cut to length: 2 strips for the ESP32-S3-Matrix, 2 for the T-Display-S3 AMOLED, 2 spare. SOCKETS not solder-down - a dead dev board in a bonded body is otherwise terminal

part: Ribbon, ground per signal - chained cluster to cluster
description: Internal looms: key chain, LED power and data, UART, power
notes: DECIDED 2026-09-21: J-CHAIN is a 2x6 IDC on a 12-way ribbon, alternating ground - GND SCK GND SH/LD GND SER GND QH GND 3V3 spare spare. TWELVE conductors per hop, chained through each cluster board in turn rather than starred, so five connectors must match: one on the carrier and one per cluster board. Every signal has ground on both sides (ADR 0001 item 1, the highest-value SI fix - these four are now the ONLY loom signals that can be corrupted and the blast radius is all 32 bits). Two spares per ADR 0009, free because IDC comes in 2xN. Chain order matters: data must flow TOWARD the clock source, so right_thumb is nearest the MCU and left_hand takes the SER end. This replaces the tail-mounted alternative's 32-44 conductors and ~46 hand-terminated joints

description: Bulk cap at the umbilical entry / buck input - the C of L-BUCK-IN's LC
notes: Completes the LC: L-BUCK-IN had an L and no C. One per buck. Also the capacitance the module load switch's inrush ramp is sized against (ADR 0005). 25V part on a 12V rail for derating

description: HF decoupling at every carrier IC - ADC, reference, buffer, level shifter, sensor
notes: One per supply pin: MCP3202, REF5050 in, OPA2197 +12V, 74AHCT125, MPXV4006DP, and both R-78E5 inputs. ADR 0001 fixed only the shift registers (C-DECOUPLE-165) and stopped there

description: Output capacitor on the REF5050
notes: Per the REF50xx datasheet's recommended output capacitance, with a 100nF from C-DECOUPLE-CARRIER alongside. This is the rail that IS the breath scale factor

description: Entry bulk capacitance downstream of each bead
notes: NOT 47uF on every rail. The +12V branch carries the LM317's divider, the DAC and the comparator, about 22mA against -12V's 10mA - so at 47uF each it collapses 2.2x faster and every rack power-down leaves the op-amps with V+ near 0 and V- at -6 to -8V for ~30ms, pulling all six jacks toward the surviving negative rail. 100uF on +12V balances the decay. 10-100uF per rail per ADR 0004; NOT the strip capacitance, which belongs at the load and is C-STRIP-BULK

description: Socket for the MPXV4006DP so the sensor is replaceable
notes: ADR 0003 calls the sensor a wear part and buys two. The spare is only reachable if the first part comes out, and the body is bonded. Case 1351-01 THT leads on 2.54mm

description: Panel power indicator
notes: A PLAIN POWER LED off the module's own rail, like every other Eurorack module's. It used to be driven by a presence comparator that watched the breath line - that comparator is DELETED, and with it the only thing in the module that tried to know whether the instrument was there. Health reporting belongs in the instrument, which has a display, a web app and the actual data. With LT1641-1 latching off on a fault, this still says why the instrument went dark

description: Series resistor for LED-PANEL
notes: ~4mA from the module's +12V analog rail. Was 820R from bus +5V when it shared a node with the level shifter's OE pins; that node is gone with the comparator

description: Breath response: log (CCW) - linear (centre) - exponential (CW)
notes: PROPOSED 2026-09-21. Same part as POT-GAIN. The centre detent is honestly warranted here and not elsewhere: at centre the wiper sits at exactly 0V by topology (it spans +Vin/2 and -Vin/2), so the nonlinear branch carries no current and the stage is mathematically linear - unlike POT-OFFSET, whose detent review found lands ~20deg off its true zero

description: Sets response curve strength
notes: PROPOSED 2026-09-21. First sizing, targeting ~1.5x gain ratio at a hard blow (4.64V at the in-amp). This is the knob that decides how strong 'fully exponential' feels and wants a bench pass with a player, not a spreadsheet

description: Nonlinear element for the response shaper
notes: PROPOSED 2026-09-21. Breath is unipolar so only one ever conducts in play; the second covers the power-on and fault excursions the 2026-09-21 review catalogued. Scaling is set at /2 so the 0.6V knee lands at about a quarter of a hard blow - at /10 it would sit ABOVE the playing range and the control would do nothing until you overblow, which was caught by checking and not by inspection

description: Response shaper: 1/2 shapes at /2 inverting, 1/2 restores x2 inverting
notes: PROPOSED 2026-09-21. This stage consumes BOTH remaining spare OPA2197 halves, so the separate A5 finding - POT-OFFSET's wiper is unbuffered, which is why its zero sits ~20deg past centre at +0.605V - needs this additional package. Both are review findings, so the package is not spare capacity being spent on a whim

part: Knob to match the pot shaft - 14mm MAX diameter
description: Knobs for the breath gain, offset and response pots
notes: Match the shaft of the POT-BREATH variant ordered - D-shaft and knurled are not interchangeable | 2026-09-21: THREE, not two - POT-RESP added. KNOB SIZE IS NOW THE BINDING CONSTRAINT: three pots across 50.50mm with 3mm gaps needs <=14mm knobs (15mm gives 51mm and does not fit). ADR 0004's claim of '16-20mm knobs' is withdrawn. 10HP buys the height back by spending the knob size 8HP was supposed to buy - three controls at 14mm beats two at 16mm, but say so honestly

part: KS-33 lighter variant - TBD at M1
description: Optional lighter-spring switches for the four left-thumb keys
notes: ADR 0002 leaves the spring weight to M1, decided by hand before anything is built. If taken, SW1-n drops by 4. Mixed weights cost nothing but a second line on the same order

description: Strap anchor through the full laminated stack
notes: Position settled empirically at the M8 pre-bond dry assembly, slightly above the centre of gravity, and not adjustable afterwards. Anchors to the PLATE STACK, never to oak

description: Internal backing plate for the etherCON and the U-bolt
notes: The D-series is rated 4mm MAX panel thickness so it cannot mount through 6mm oak. The oak is the face the screws pass through, not the thing they hold

description: Thumb switch plate, mounted to the inside face of the oak bottom
notes: Carries the 4 left-thumb and 3 right-thumb switches. Same 14.0 x 14.0mm cutout geometry, same vendor and same order as PLATE-TOP

description: Laminated thumb rest lip on the bottom panel
notes: A 2D part added by lamination - there is no pocketing anywhere in this design. The right thumb rests here and RT1-3 sit offset from the rest position

description: Pull-up on every 74x165 key input
notes: 2k2. The 10k this started at was fine for a register beside its switch, and the 2k2 was chosen when the node ran 265mm down an UNCOATED loom - that reason is gone now the register is back on the cluster board. Kept anyway as cheap insurance: the cavity is still breathed into for hours at 10-20K above ambient and the switch contacts are still open, and 1.5mA per PRESSED key against a 360mA budget is nothing. TWENTY-FOUR: one per switch position including the 3 spare-switch bits, PLUS one each for the 3 genuinely free bits (22, 23, 31) which the first cluster-board draft left floating - the exact ADR 0001 fix-6 fault, and unretrofittable

description: Series resistor between each switch and its 74x165 input
notes: With C-KEY: press is ~1us (100R x 10nF) so it stays instant, release is ~93us (10k x 10nF) which is a free hardware debounce. Also bounds injected current

description: Filter cap at each 74x165 key input
notes: 47nF with the 2k2 pull-up keeps tau at ~103us, the same release filter as the old 10k/10nF pair. Press crosses HC165's VIL (0.99V at 3.3V) in ~5.7us, so 'press is instant' survives - 44x margin against the 250us scan period. Release crosses VIH (2.31V) at ~125us. The '~1.4us / 176x' pair this row used to carry was the 10nF part against LVC thresholds; both changed. NOTE the coupling argument that originally justified this part was wrong (see ADR 0001): a capacitive divider cannot exceed the aggressor's swing, and on the real 5V data line an unfiltered wire sees 1.36V, which does not cross a 0.8V threshold. The filter is cheap insurance and a bounce filter, not the thing that makes the topology safe

description: Key chain connector - carrier and cluster boards
notes: DECIDED 2026-09-21. Pinout GND SCK GND SH/LD GND SER GND QH GND 3V3 spare spare - a ground between every signal (ADR 0001 item 1). EIGHT of them, not five: the chain is four hops and SER/QH are point-to-point rather than bus, so every cluster board but the last carries an IN and an OUT. Carrier 1, right_thumb 2, right_hand 2, left_thumb 2, left_hand 1, with four ribbon assemblies between. BOXED AND KEYED because a reversed chain connector puts 3V3 into QH. Same pinout at all eight

description: Series damping at the chain driving end on SCK, SH/LD and SER
notes: PROPOSED by cluster-boards.md and carrier.md and never given a row until 2026-09-21. Edge-rate damping at the source, which is a DIFFERENT job from the R-TERM-CHAIN that ADR 0001 deleted - that was series TERMINATION, wrong for a line dropping on four boards. Same 100R as R-SPI-SER

description: ESD protection on the key chain signals leaving the carrier
notes: PROPOSED by carrier.md and never given a row until 2026-09-21. The chain's four signals leave the board and run the length of the body. U-TVS-SPI does exactly this job for the umbilical's three

description: Fuse on the 3V3 conductor feeding the cluster boards
notes: PROPOSED by carrier.md and never given a row until 2026-09-21. The 3V3 conductor runs 265mm through a bonded body beside 12V LED power; a short on it browns out the dev board LDO and takes the instrument down with no diagnosis. Two millimetres of board, unretrofittable

description: Console header: U0TXD, U0RXD, GND for each board
notes: SIX pins, not ten. EN and IO0 are NOT available: the vendor's board definition accounts for every pin on the ESP32-S3-Matrix's two header rows (3 power + 17 GPIO) and neither appears. They exist on the board - IO0 under the BOOT button, EN on the reset circuit - but reaching them means soldering to the dev board, which ends its life as a swappable module. This is the THIRD line of defence anyway: OTA rollback first, then USB-Serial-JTAG through the tail USB-C slot (which is why USB MIDI is opt-in), then this. A corrupted BOOTLOADER ends the instrument; that is accepted

description: Removable cover over HDR-SERVICE on the tail underside
notes: Same laminated layer as the matrix window, beside it. Screws into the plate stack, not the oak. Goes into the M4 CAD with the window and the etherCON backing plate, and into the 1:1 paper check of the tail face

description: ESD protection on the umbilical's SPI lines
notes: SCLK, MOSI, CS (+ one spare channel) to PWR_GND. REPLACES U-TVS-UMB, which named SP3012-06UTG: that part is obsolete AND uDFN-14, not the SOT-23-6 the row claimed - leadless fine pitch, banned by the ADR 0013 package policy. It was un-orderable as written

description: ESD protection on the BREATH and AGND legs
notes: 12V STANDOFF, NOT 5V. BREATH's normal top of range is 4.7V against a 5V array's V_RWM - 300mV of margin on the project's DC-accurate output, with 1.5uA of leakage into a 1k output resistor. Worse, ADR 0003's buffer-on-+12V decision exists precisely so a SUSTAINED +12V fault on BREATH is harmless; a 5V clamp would turn that designed-safe case into a part that conducts until something fails

description: TVS across the umbilical power pair at the instrument
notes: 15V standoff on a 12V rail. The power pair is the one the old 6-channel array could never have covered - six channels against eight conductors, and the six non-power ones are the natural fit

part: Same three groups, module end of the etherCON
description: ESD protection at the module end of the umbilical
notes: The BOM had protection at one end only. DELIBERATELY open, not forgotten: the module is behind four screws and this is retrofittable, where the instrument end is bonded shut. Fit at E12 if E11 gives any reason to

description: Shunt diode across the umbilical power pair at the instrument
notes: UNRETROFITTABLE. A rollover/console RJ45 lead swaps 3 and 6, which on the T568B map are +12V and PWR_GND - reverse polarity into a bonded instrument, from a consumable patch lead that looks identical to a good one. Cathode to the +12V pin: reversed, it conducts hard, the module's LT1641-1 sees a short and LATCHES OFF, and the panel LED says so. The load switch becomes the fuse

description: Oak-to-oak lamination: spacer layers and the thumb rest lip
notes: The only wood-to-wood joints in the stack, and the strongest and cheapest joint available. Does NOT bond aluminium or acrylic, which is half the reason the old single MECH-ADHESIVE row could not have worked

part: RTV silicone - ALKOXY (alcohol) neutral cure, electronics-safe
description: Everything that is not wood-to-wood: plate to oak, acrylic sides, matrix diffuser, thumb plate
notes: NOT ACETOXY. The common hardware-store type releases acetic acid while curing, inside a sealed cavity holding two dev boards, a carrier, connectors and a pressure sensor. Compliant in shear so the oak's 0.6-0.9mm of cross-grain humidity movement does not fight the aluminium plate; stiff in compression so the plate is still backed under a key press. BEAD IT, DO NOT BUTTER IT - cure needs atmospheric moisture and runs ~2mm/day inwards, so a trapped full-face layer never cures. Keep it off both sensor ports (ADR 0003)

description: Pitch gain trimmer, in series with R2 of the LT5400 pair
notes: 200R, not 1k. In series with R2 it is 0 to +2% of the ratio, and its ~100ppm/degC then contributes ~2ppm/degC - COMPARABLE to the LT5400 rather than 4-20x it, which was ADR 0006's own objection to its own trimmer. Two percent is enough now that pitch feedback is tapped at the jack and the load divider is gone; firmware's per-load affine covers the remainder

description: Pitch offset trimmer, AHEAD of the VREFOUT follower
notes: MOVED. It now trims the reference the follower buffers, so it scales the intercept (k x V_ref) and touches the gain (1 + k) NOT AT ALL - a genuinely independent offset trim. R-OFFINJ is deleted with it: injecting into the inverting node was never a pure offset, because in a non-inverting stage that node sits at Vdac rather than at a virtual ground, so it added ~1% of gain and its span was one-sided. Range ~50mV on a 2.5V reference is ~60 cents of offset

description: Compensation cap, op-amp OUTPUT to the inverting input
notes: FROM THE OP-AMP OUTPUT TO THE (-) INPUT. NOT 'across the feedback resistor' - with the tap at the jack, R2 spans jack-to-(-), so a cap across R2 connects the same two nodes and leaves R-OUT-PROT inside the loop at every frequency: 18 degrees of phase margin with 2m of cable, under 10 with four destinations. Three documents said 'across R2' and were wrong. 2.2nF with C-FILT-PITCH restored is maximally flat, -3dB at 12.2kHz. IT IS NOT A FILTER: a cap in the feedback of a NON-INVERTING stage gives (2+sRC)/(1+sRC), a pole and a zero an octave up, flattening at unity - 6.02dB maximum for any value. Two independent reviews found this separately

part: 10k multiturn cermet + divider from the LM317 5.21V rail
description: Nulls the sensor's +0.2V pedestal at the INA828 REF pin
notes: Buffered by a half of U-OPA-PITCH - REF needs a low source impedance or it degrades CMRR one-for-one. RANGE 0 TO +1.0V, not the 0-0.6V first specified. The pedestal is a SPEC BAND, 0.152-0.378V, not the 0.200V typical: nulling the top of it needs 0.826V at REF, and a 0.6V ceiling covers only 0.275V of pedestal. A part at the top of its own spec would have been un-nullable, leaving 1.4-5.6% of span standing at the jack - the same band as the polarity showstopper this trimmer replaced. +1.0V covers 0.458V with margin. FROM THE LM317'S 5.21V, NOT VREFOUT. VREFOUT is the DAC's internal reference, which is DISABLED at power-on until firmware writes an enable - so deriving the breath zero from it would make the analog breath path depend on a DAC register, which three documents correctly say it does not. The LM317 rail is up whenever +12V is. THIS IS WHAT MAKES THE PANEL KNOBS INDEPENDENT: with REF grounded the pedestal sits upstream of the gain pot and gets multiplied. One zero authority per representation still holds: this is CALIBRATION, set once, where the panel OFFSET knob is PERFORMANCE

description: Per cluster: switches, one 74HC165, its decoupling, and the per-key network
notes: One per cluster - left hand (5), left thumb (4), right hand (6), right thumb (3). The switches need a rigid PCB regardless (ADR 0002), so putting the register on it is nearly free: every switch-to-chip connection becomes a TRACE and TWELVE conductors leave each board on a 2x6 IDC. That is ~8 connectors across 4 ribbon assemblies of hand work against ~46 individual wires for the tail-mounted alternative, and it keeps 63 passives off the carrier

description: Selects the 74HC165 serial-input source on each cluster board
notes: PROPOSED by hardware/controller/cluster-boards.md. Position A on the three boards that have an OUT connector: SER comes from the next board's QH. Position B on the chain-end board: SER comes from the IN pin 6 passthrough, which reaches the carrier. One link is what lets all four boards be ONE schematic instead of a special last variant

description: Pull-up on the chain-end board serial input
notes: PROPOSED by hardware/controller/cluster-boards.md. Chain-end board only. Holds the far serial input high when nothing drives it, which is the tied-off case ADR 0001 specified. If firmware instead DRIVES it from the carrier's IO33, the 100R series wins against 10k to within 33mV of the rail - so an end-to-end chain self-test (shift a known pattern through all 32 bits, distinguishing a broken loom from a stuck bit) becomes a FIRMWARE choice rather than a board choice, for one resistor

description: Series resistor on each WS2815 data line at the driver
notes: TWO PARTS ON THE AGGRESSOR, against 63 on the victims. Standard practice at an addressable-LED driver: damps the fastest edge in the instrument at its source and protects the 74AHCT125 output. FOUR not two: the WS2815's BACKUP data line is cited as a reason for the part choice in ADR 0014 and again in ADR 0005, and was connected to nothing - the level shifter's two spare gates are exactly what it needs

description: Anti-alias/glitch filter on the pitch DAC input, ahead of the op-amp
notes: THE ACTUAL PITCH FILTER. 15.9kHz against R-OPAMP-IN's 1k, on a node with NO LOOP AROUND IT. C-FB-PITCH cannot do this job: a cap across the feedback resistor of a NON-INVERTING stage gives (2+sRC)/(1+sRC) - a pole at 15.9kHz and a zero an octave above, flattening at unity, so 6.02dB of attenuation maximum for any value. It is a shelf, not a pole. Filtering the DAC before the stage is also what the surveyed designs do

description: Fault timer capacitor for U-LOADSW
notes: BLOCKING. 10nF was wrong by 12x to 300x and gave a 0.16-4ms fault timer, so the module latched off at the end of every start. Three reviewers found this independently. C = I_TIMER x t / 1.233V; target t = 150ms, which is 2.4x the ~62ms current-limited start that foldback forces. That is 365nF if I_TIMER is 3uA and 9.25uF if it is 76uA - the reviewers disagree and the datasheet decides. READ THE LT1641 DATASHEET BEFORE ORDERING. The old 0805 C0G package is wrong for any value in that range

description: Gate capacitor programming the load switch ramp
notes: BLOCKING, AND IT DID NOT EXIST. There was no gate capacitor in the BOM or the schematic, yet the FET sizing, the boot analysis and ADR 0005's 50-100ms ramp specification all rest on a 'programmed ramp'. With the FET's bare Ciss (~1nF) and ~10uA of gate current the ramp is 10kV/s, which demands 2.2mF x 10kV/s = 22A - twenty-odd times the limit. C = I_GATE / (dV/dt); a 100ms ramp is 120V/s, so ~83nF at 10uA. READ I_GATE OFF THE LT1641 DATASHEET BEFORE ORDERING

description: Clamp diodes on the BREATH and AGND legs at the in-amp inputs
notes: Drawn on hardware/module/breath-receive-stage.md and had no row. Silicon, to +-12V, behind the 10k series resistors. Distinct from D-TVS-BREATH, which is the ESD part at the connector

part: Range-setting resistors for the two module trimmers
description: Sets TRIM-OFFSET's and TRIM-BREATH-ZERO's spans
notes: Both trimmers need a divider to set their span and neither had parts. TRIM-OFFSET wants ~+-50mV around 2.500V; TRIM-BREATH-ZERO wants 0 to +1.0V from the LM317 rail. Values with the stages at E10

description: Reconstruction and RF shunt at the pitch jack
notes: RESTORED. It was deleted on the reasoning that a cap on the feedback node sits inside the DC loop at the handover; two independent loop analyses then put 10nF there and found phase margin UNCHANGED, because C-FB-PITCH ties the (-) input to the op-amp OUTPUT so beta(inf)=1 and R-OUT-PROT isolates the jack above the handover. The feedback network is a LEAD at every load tried - open, 200pF, 800pF, 10nF, dead short. Deleting it cost 30dB at 1MHz and left the connector with no low-impedance shunt at all

description: DC bias path to ground at every DAC output pin
notes: AT THE DAC PIN, not after R-OPAMP-IN - 100k after the 1k would form a divider and cost 1% of gain. Without it the op-amp (+) inputs have no DC path to ground: their only connection is a DAC pin that may be high-Z before power-on reset, so outputs can sit at either rail during that window. The identical problem was already found and fixed on the breath in-amp (R-BIAS-INAMP); this is the same fix on the six DAC-driven nodes

description: Ties the DAC8568 LDAC pin to its inactive level
notes: LDAC appeared NOWHERE in the design, which left a CMOS input floating on the DAC. Tied, not driven: a hardware LDAC was considered and declined, and six channels therefore cannot update atomically - every exit from CLR throws intermediate values at the mod jacks for 100-200us and no write order avoids it. If E10 finds that audible, this becomes a GPIO and the pin is already broken out

description: Isolation resistor inside the REF5050 buffer's feedback loop
notes: INSIDE THE LOOP, with feedback taken at the SENSOR's VS pin - so the DC error is zero and the capacitive load is isolated from the op-amp's output. Outside the loop the same resistor would cost 2% of the ratiometric scale factor. Without it the follower drives 100nF + 10uF directly: a 21kHz pole inside a loop crossing at MHz. This lands on the sensor's EXCITATION, i.e. on its scale factor, and the other half of that package is the breath buffer

description: Spare dev boards, bought with the originals
notes: BUY THEM WITH THE ORIGINALS, not later. ADR 0013 names a discontinued dev board as a redesign risk and both vendors ship silent revisions. A spare does NOT rescue a bricked instrument once the body is bonded - it cannot get in - so this is insurance against a dead board during BUILD and bring-up, and against the part vanishing before M8

description: Panel breath GAIN - attenuator ahead of the summer
notes: Attenuator, NOT a feedback rheostat - a rheostat makes gain and offset share a resistor and the knobs fight, which is the coupling the REF trimmer was added to remove one stage upstream. 0.125 to 1.000 against a fixed x4 = 0.5 to 4.0 at the jack. WIPER MUST BE BUFFERED: it drives R-IN, so an unbuffered wiper makes the gain depend on a source impedance that varies with rotation. Taper is a feel question and therefore a bench question

description: Panel breath OFFSET - bipolar, zero at centre
notes: +-5V at the jack with ZERO AT CENTRE: CCW +5.04V, centre +0.07V, CW -4.89V. Wiper does NOT need buffering - source impedance is 0 at both ends and R/4 at centre, so the endpoints are exact and the middle is slightly non-linear in rotation, which for an offset knob is feel rather than error. A centre-detent variant would make 'no offset' findable in the dark; E10 call

description: Sets the 0.5x floor of POT-GAIN's attenuator
notes: 7.15k under a 50k track gives 7.15/57.15 = 0.125, so the gain bottoms at 0.5x rather than zero. Without it the knob reaches a mute nobody asked for and an easy way to think the instrument is dead

description: Summer input and feedback - the fixed x4
notes: R-IN 10k, R-FB 40.2k. Same E96 feedback part as R-MODGAIN, bought on the same reel

description: The two offset legs into the summing node
notes: R-OFF 21.0k from the buffered 5.21V wiper (variable, positive), R-OFFNEG 95.3k from -12V (fixed, negative). Their sum crosses zero at mid-rotation. NO extra op-amp half and no negative reference to generate, which is what makes +-5V cost two resistors. -12V is acceptable HERE where it was not for pitch: 50mV of rail movement is 21mV at the jack, 0.21% of span, and the -12V rail carries no LED current because the strips run from +12V
